title: Mass spectrometry and machine learning identify bioactive peptide NHPD-50
summary: A predicted-peptide-variant model trained using mass-spectrometry observations from seven mouse tissues helped prioritize candidate peptides. The authors report that NHPD-50, a secretogranin-1-derived peptide, lowered blood glucose and increased plasma insulin in specified diabetic-mouse experiments. The authors state that the data do not establish the peptide’s exact mechanism. These are early preclinical findings, not a human diabetes treatment; other predicted peptides had different or absent outcomes.
ai_technology: Predicted-peptide-variant machine-learning prioritization from mass-spectrometry data

source_review.scope: Primary Nature full article and bibliographic metadata reviewed for identity, AI role, date, affiliation and bounded mouse results.

evidence.tested: Primary paper reports the stated mouse assay results.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and exhaustive prior-art review are not established; the paper states that the mechanism is undetermined.
evidence.ai_role: A predicted-peptide-variant model prioritized candidate sequences from mass-spectrometry data; biological activity was established through subsequent assays.
